BOUNDS, FIXED BEFORE THE FIRST MEASUREMENT OF THE CHANGED CODE (the unchanged 16f5190 had been
measured for hashes and the memory table; no changed code had run). Never loosened afterwards.

B1 outputs: every embedding hash (profile_embedgemma2 PROFILE_MODE=hash: 6 workloads x 2 operand
   modes x {full, truncate_dim 128}) and the tiny-model hashes equal the 16f5190 ones, bit for bit.
   A component whose hashes differ is not shipped unless the difference is explained and the
   user-visible numerics bounds of the existing tests still hold.
B2 memory (deterministic, fresh process per cell):
   a. back-to-back peak == single-encode peak, within 0.5 MiB, for every workload and mode;
   b. the activation set at 8192 rows (single peak at 32x256, 8x1024, 2x4096) <= 736 - 240 (PLE at
      16 MiB) - 96 (qkv aliased with gate|up) + 1 = 400 MiB, f32 mode;
   c. every cell is <= its 16f5190 value (+0.5 MiB), never above.
B3 time (bench_embedgemma2 lanes through bench_paired, order reversed on odd rounds, >= 6 rounds,
   each lane's workload value is min of BENCH_ITERS iterations): for every workload and both
   precisions, the median over rounds of lane/before is <= 1.03. The GPU spread between rounds
   (max/min of the ratio series) is reported; a series over 1.25 is repeated, not accepted.
B4 PLE default: the smallest of {16 MiB, 64 MiB} whose lane/ple256 median ratio is <= 1.03 at all
   five uniform workloads in both precisions; if neither passes the default stays 256 MiB.

B4 (amended before the sweep below ran; a stricter condition added, none removed): the median-of-round-ratios rule above is on a machine whose
rounds spread 2-30x (load average 100+ on 18 cores, other lanes on the GPU), and in two independent runs the min-of-N ratio of the 16 MiB
bound at 64x32 (2048 rows, 4 layers per run) read 1.045 and 1.074 against 256 MiB, while the medians read 0.965 and 1.002. So the default is
accepted only if BOTH statistics (median of 12 round ratios, min-of-N ratio) are <= 1.03 against 256 MiB at 1024, 2048 and 4096 rows
(32x32, 64x32, 128x32, a dedicated 12-round, 3-lane sweep, BENCH_ITERS=20) and in the earlier runs at the 8192-row workloads.
Order of preference: 16 MiB, then 64 MiB, then 256 MiB unchanged.

B4 repeat rule (declared after the f32 8192-row sweep read 1.0303 at 2x4096, median of 8 rounds, spread 1.75, against the 1.03 limit; and after the first bf16 1024-4096-row sweep ran at load 14-38 per core with spreads of 2.2-4.6):
a cell over the limit on a series whose spread exceeds 1.25 is repeated once, with 12 rounds where the series was 8, using the same two statistics; the repeat decides. Two repeats were run; no other cell was repeated.
Noise floor ≤ 5 % — measured on an M5 Pro 😀
